Below is a clear, periodized 12-week strength + hypertrophy program starting 2026-06-01 (Monday). It blends evidence-based hypertrophy volume with progressive strength work, balanced movement patterns, and built-in deloads. Designed for a healthy 26-year-old recreational lifter on a combined oral contraceptive (no cycle-based adjustments needed).

Overview
- Goal: Add muscle (hypertrophy) while increasing foundational strength in squat, deadlift, bench, and overhead press; improve work capacity.
- Structure: 4 lifting days/week + 1–2 low-impact conditioning + daily mobility. Total 12 weeks in 3 phases with a deload.
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy base + technique (moderate loads, higher volumes).
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength emphasis with hypertrophy back-off (heavier compounds, moderate volume).
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification and peak strength with strategic deload in Week 9, finish with rep PRs/AMRAP caps in Week 12.
- Split:
  - Day 1: Lower A (Squat focus)
  - Day 2: Upper A (Bench focus)
  - Day 3: Lower B (Hinge/Deadlift focus)
  - Day 4: Upper B (Overhead/Row focus)
- Conditioning: 1–2 sessions/week (Zone 2 and/or tempo intervals)
- Progression: Double progression (rep then load) on accessories; percentage/RPE on main lifts.
- RPE guide: Accessories RPE 7–9; compounds as noted.
- Warm-up: 5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility + specific ramp-up sets.
- Cooldown: Easy cyclical 5 min + stretch key tissues 5–8 min.

Key Terms
- RIR = Reps in reserve
- RPE 7 ≈ 3 RIR; RPE 8 ≈ 2 RIR; RPE 9 ≈ 1 RIR
- Tempo notation: e.g., 3-0-1 = 3s eccentric, no pause, 1s concentric.
- Rest: Compounds 2–3 min; accessories 60–90s unless noted.

Testing/Estimations
- If no current 1RMs, estimate from recent 5–10RM sets. Adjust loads by RPE on Day 1; the plan uses % as anchors but RPE governs decisions.

Weekly Template
- Mon: Lower A
- Tue: Upper A
- Thu: Lower B
- Fri: Upper B
- Wed/Sat: Optional conditioning/mobility
- Sun: Rest

Phase 1: Foundation Hypertrophy + Technique (Weeks 1–4)
Intent: Build volume tolerance, refine technique, add muscle. Moderate loads, controlled tempo, higher reps.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07)
- Lower A (Squat focus)
  - Back Squat 4×6 @ ~70% 1RM (RPE 7–8)
  - Romanian Deadlift 3×8 @ RPE 7–8
  - Split Squat (DB) 3×10/side @ RPE 8
  - Leg Curl (seated/lying) 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Standing Calf Raise 3×12–15 @ RPE 8
  - Core: Hanging Knee Raise 3×10–12
- Upper A (Bench focus)
  - Barbell Bench Press 4×6 @ ~70% (RPE 7–8)
  - One-Arm DB Row 3×10/side @ RPE 8
  - Incline DB Bench 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral) 3×10–12 @ RPE 8
  - Cable Lateral Raise 3×12–15 @ RPE 8
  - Triceps Rope Pressdown 2–3×12
- Lower B (Hinge focus)
  - Conventional Deadlift 4×4 @ ~72–75% (RPE 7–8)
  - Front Squat 3×6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Hip Thrust (barbell) 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - Back Extension or 45° Hyper 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Seated Calf Raise 3×12–15
  - Core: Cable Pallof Press 3×10–12/side
- Upper B (Overhead/Row focus)
  - Overhead Press (barbell) 4×5 @ ~70% (RPE 7–8)
  - Pull-Up or Assisted 4×6–8 (leave 2 RIR)
  - Chest-Supported Row 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - DB Incline Fly or Cable Fly 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Face Pull 3×12–15
  - EZ-Bar Curl 2–3×10–12

Week 2
- Progress accessories via double progression: add 1–2 reps per set (stay within rep ranges) or +2–5% load if all top-end reps were met last week.
- Compounds: +2.5% load if Week 1 was ≤RPE 8; otherwise keep load and add one rep per top set if appropriate (e.g., 4×7 instead of 4×6 on squats/bench), cap at RPE 9.
- Keep same exercise selection as Week 1.

Week 3
- Compounds: 4×7 @ ~72–73% (squat/bench), deadlift 4×5 @ 75–77%, OHP 4×6 @ 72–73%. Aim RPE 8.
- Accessories: Nudge load or reps again; keep 1–2 reps in reserve.

Week 4
- Slight overload week before transition.
- Squat 5×6 @ 72–75% (top set RPE 8.5), Bench 5×6 @ 72–75%, Deadlift 5×4 @ 77–78%, OHP 5×5 @ 73–75%.
- Keep accessories at Week 3 loads but hold reps steady (do not chase failure). Focus on quality and bracing.

Phase 2: Strength Emphasis + Hypertrophy Support (Weeks 5–8)
Intent: Heavier compounds, moderate volume; maintain hypertrophy with accessories (8–12 reps).

Week 5
- Lower A
  - Back Squat 5×4 @ 77–80% (RPE 8)
  - Pause Squat (2s) 3×3 @ ~70%
  - RDL 3×8 @ RPE 8
  - Walking Lunge (DB) 3×10/leg
  - Leg Curl 3×10–12
  - Ab Wheel 3×8–10
- Upper A
  - Bench Press 5×4 @ 77–80% (RPE 8)
  - 2-Count Paused Bench 3×3 @ ~72%
  - Chest-Supported Row 4×8 @ RPE 8
  - Incline DB Bench 3×8–10
  - Lateral Raise 3×12–15
  - Triceps Pressdown 3×10–12
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 5×3 @ 80–83% (RPE 8)
  - Deficit Deadlift (1–2") 3×3 @ ~70–72%
  - Front Squat 3×5 @ RPE 8
  - Hip Thrust 3×8–10
  - Back Extension 3×10–12
  - Side Plank 3×30–45s/side
- Upper B
  - Overhead Press 5×3 @ 78–80% (RPE 8)
  - Push Press 3×3 @ ~75–80% of OHP
  - Pull-Up 4×6–8 (add load if able; leave 1–2 RIR)
  - Single-Arm Cable Row 3×10/side
  - Face Pull 3×12–15
  - DB Curl 3×10–12

Week 6
- Compounds: +2.5% if Week 5 RPE ≤8; otherwise match load and add 1 rep to first set only if form is pristine.
- Accessories: Progress load 2–5% or add 1–2 reps.
- Keep same exercise menu.

Week 7
- Slight intensity bump; reduce sets where needed to manage fatigue.
  - Squat 4×4 @ 80–82%
  - Bench 4×4 @ 80–82%
  - Deadlift 4×3 @ 82–85% (no grinders)
  - OHP 4×3 @ 80–82%
- Accessories: Maintain or slightly reduce volume (one fewer set on smaller muscles) to prioritize recovery.

Week 8
- Strength overload before deload next week.
  - Squat 5×3 @ 82–85% (top set RPE 8.5)
  - Bench 5×3 @ 82–85%
  - Deadlift 5×2 @ 85–87%
  - OHP 5×2–3 @ 82–85%
- Accessories: Keep to lower end of sets; stop at 1–2 RIR. Extra mobility work.

Phase 3: Intensification + Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Intent: Deload to shed fatigue, then push heavy top sets with submax back-off for strength, maintain hypertrophy with targeted accessories. Conclude with controlled AMRAP caps/reps PRs.

Week 9 (Deload)
- Reduce volume ~40–50% and intensity to ~60–65% on compounds; accessories 1–2 sets each at RPE 6–7.
  - Squat 3×3 @ 60–65%
  - Bench 3×3 @ 60–65%
  - Deadlift 3×2 @ 60–65%
  - OHP 3×3 @ 60–65%
  - Light rows, lunges, curls, laterals 1–2×12
- Extra: Mobility, light cardio, sleep focus.

Week 10
- Top set + back-off model (strength priority).
  - Squat: Top set 1×3 @ ~85–88% (RPE ~8.5), then 3×4 @ 80%
  - Bench: Top set 1×3 @ 85–88%, then 3×4 @ 80%
  - Deadlift: Top set 1×2–3 @ 87–90%, then 3×3 @ 80–82%
  - OHP: Top set 1×3 @ 85%, then 3×4 @ 78–80%
- Accessories (keep pump, not fatigue):
  - Quads: Hack squat or leg press 2–3×8–10
  - Hams: Leg curl 2–3×10–12
  - Chest: Incline DB 2–3×8–10
  - Back: Chest-supported row 2–3×8–10
  - Delts/arms: Lateral raise + rope pressdown + curl 2×12–15 each
  - Core: Choose 1–2 moves 2–3 sets

Week 11
- Slight progression from Week 10.
  - Squat: Top 1×2–3 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3–4 @ 80–82%
  - Bench: Top 1×2–3 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3–4 @ 80–82%
  - Deadlift: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 82–85%
  - OHP: Top 1×2–3 @ 87–88%, back-off 3×3 @ 80–82%
- Accessories: Same as Week 10, keep 1–2 RIR.

Week 12 (Cap with rep PRs, not true 1RMs)
- Goal: Demonstrate progress with safe AMRAP caps; no grinders beyond RPE 9.
  - Squat: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% cap 5–6 reps, stop at RPE 9; then 2×3 @ 80%
  - Bench: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% cap 6–7 reps; then 2×3 @ 80%
  - Deadlift: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% cap 4–5 reps; then 2×2 @ 80%
  - OHP: 1×AMRAP @ ~82–85% cap 5–6 reps; then 2×3 @ 78–80%
- Minimal accessories: 1–2 light pump sets per muscle if desired.
- Optional: Estimate new 1RMs via Epley from AMRAPs.

Conditioning, Mobility, and Recovery (Weeks 1–12)
- Conditioning
  - 1–2 sessions/week, 20–30 min.
  - Option A: Zone 2 steady (RPE 4–5) cycling/row/jog.
  - Option B: Tempo intervals 6–8×1 min @ RPE 7 with 1–2 min easy between.
  - Keep high-intensity work 24–36h away from lower-body heavy days.
- Daily Mobility (8–12 min)
  - Prioritize hips, T-spine, ankles, shoulders.
  - Example flow: 90/90 hip switches, couch stretch, ankle rocks, T-spine rotations, pec doorway stretch.
- Warm-Up (each lift day)
  - 5–8 min easy cardio, movement prep (hip airplanes, band pull-aparts, scapular pull-ups), then specific ramp-ups: e.g., Squat 5 reps @ bar, 5 @ 40%, 3 @ 60%, 2 @ 70% to work weight.
- Sleep/Stress
  - 7–9 hours/night, consistent schedule; manage stress to support recovery.
- Steps/NEAT
  - Target 7–10k steps/day if compatible with recovery.

Load Progression Rules
- Main lifts:
  - If last set ≤RPE 8 and all prescribed reps completed, add 2.5–5 lb (1–2.5 kg) upper body; 5–10 lb (2.5–5 kg) lower body next exposure.
  - If RPE 9–9.5 or reps missed, repeat load next week or reduce 2.5–5%.
- Accessories:
  - Progress via double progression; when top of rep range hit across sets with 1–2 RIR, add the smallest load increment next week.
- Technique first: No maxing. Bar speed should be consistent until Week 12 AMRAP sets.

Injury-Prevention/Technique Emphases
- Brace and breath: Val Salva on heavy reps as appropriate; maintain neutral spine.
- Range: Aim full ROM without pain; tempo control on eccentrics (2–3s).
- Variation: Pauses and deficits used for positional strength; rotate only as programmed.

Nutrition (general guidance; adjust to client specifics)
- Calories: Mild surplus for hypertrophy if body comp allows (+200–300 kcal/day). If maintenance preferred, prioritize progressive overload and adequate protein.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day spread over 3–5 meals; include 20–40 g high-quality protein within 1–2 hours pre/post training.
- Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day; center carbs around training (pre + post) to support performance.
- Fats: 0.7–1.0 g/kg/day; include essential fats. No specific adjustments needed for COC here.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add 500–1000 ml around training. Consider electrolytes in hot/humid conditions.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, daily, safe and effective for women; no cycling needed.
- Caffeine: 1.5–3 mg/kg 30–60 min pre-workout if desired; avoid late-day intake.
- Fiber/micronutrients: 25–35 g fiber/day; fruits/veg 5+ servings; ensure calcium/vitamin D sufficiency.

Weekly Check-ins and Auto-Regulation
- Rate session RPE, sleep, soreness (0–10).
- If two consecutive sessions feel ≥2 points worse than baseline, reduce accessory volume by 20–30% for the week and maintain loads.
- If a single lift stalls for 2 weeks, take a small reset: drop 5% and build back up.

Example Week Schedule (Week 1)
- Mon 06/01: Lower A
- Tue 06/02: Upper A
- Wed 06/03: Zone 2 25 min + mobility
- Thu 06/04: Lower B
- Fri 06/05: Upper B
- Sat 06/06: Optional tempo intervals 6×1 min + mobility
- Sun 06/07: Rest

By following the week-by-week structure above, you can coach progressive overload with clear guardrails, keep fatigue managed through a planned deload, and finish with measurable progress markers in Week 12. Adjust loads each week using RPE and the progression rules to fit the client’s day-to-day readiness.

Here’s a practical hypertrophy-supportive nutrition plan you can plug in alongside the 12-week program. It includes calorie targets, macro ranges, timing, food templates, and progression checks. Adjust numbers based on the client’s current body size and preferences.

1) Set calories for a lean surplus
- Target: +200–300 kcal/day above true maintenance to gain ~0.25–0.5% bodyweight per week.
- How to find maintenance quickly:
  - If you have a recent stable-intake baseline, use that as maintenance.
  - Or estimate: 32–36 kcal/kg bodyweight as a starting point for active women, then refine using weekly scale trends.
- Weekly adjustment rule:
  - If average weekly weight change <0.15% BW for 2 consecutive weeks and training performance is good: +80–120 kcal/day.
  - If weight gain >0.6% BW/week for 2 consecutive weeks or fatigue/appetite poor: −80–120 kcal/day.

2) Protein, carbs, fats (daily macro targets)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
  - Aim for the middle initially: ~1.8–2.0 g/kg/day.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day (do not go below 0.7 g/kg for hormonal health and satiety).
- Carbohydrate: Fill remaining calories with carbs (usually lands around 3–6 g/kg/day in surplus for active lifters).
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from whole foods.

Example macro setup (for a 65 kg client; adjust proportionally)
- Calories: Maintenance ~2,200 kcal → Surplus target ~2,450 kcal.
- Protein: 2.0 g/kg = 130 g (520 kcal)
- Fat: 0.9 g/kg = 60 g (540 kcal)
- Carbs: Remaining kcal ≈ 2,450 − (520 + 540) = 1,390 kcal → 348 g carbs
- Ranges to allow flexibility:
  - Protein 120–140 g
  - Fat 50–70 g
  - Carbs 300–380 g

3) Nutrient timing around training
- Pre-workout (1–2 hours before):
  - 30–60 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; low fat/fiber to reduce GI distress.
  - Examples: Greek yogurt + fruit; turkey sandwich; whey + banana; rice cakes + cottage cheese.
- Intra (optional if >75–90 min hard training or hot conditions):
  - 20–40 g fast carbs + electrolytes; 5–10 g essential amino acids or 10–15 g whey if last meal was >3 hours ago.
- Post-workout (0–2 hours after):
  - 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; a small amount of fat is fine.
  - Examples: Rice + chicken + veg; oats + whey + berries; chocolate milk + trail mix (small handful).
- Daily protein distribution:
  - 3–5 feedings with 20–40 g high-quality protein each, plus a pre-sleep protein dose (20–40 g casein-rich food) to support overnight MPS.

4) Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: ~30–40 ml/kg/day baseline + 500–1,000 ml around training.
- Add 300–500 mg sodium pre-workout if sessions are sweaty or in heat; consider a simple electrolyte mix (300–600 mg Na, 100–200 mg K, 50–100 mg Mg).

5) Supplement strategy (optional but effective)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily, any time, no cycling.
- Vitamin D3: 1,000–2,000 IU/day if levels unknown/low; confirm with labs when possible.
- Fish oil (EPA/DHA): 1–2 g combined EPA+DHA/day if oily fish intake is low.
- Caffeine: 1.5–3 mg/kg 30–60 min pre-workout if desired; avoid within 8 hours of bedtime.
- Whey/casein: Convenience to hit protein targets; not required.
- Beta-alanine (optional for higher-rep work): 3.2–6.4 g/day in divided doses; expect paresthesia.

6) Meal templates (plug-and-play)
- Breakfast options
  - Oats cooked in milk + whey + berries + peanut butter
  - Eggs (2–3) + egg whites + wholegrain toast + avocado + fruit
  - Greek yogurt parfait: yogurt + granola + banana + honey + chia
- Lunch options
  - Rice/quinoa + chicken/thigh or tofu/tempeh + veggies + olive oil
  - Wholegrain wrap with lean beef/turkey + hummus + salad + fruit
  - Pasta + tuna or chicken + marinara + parmesan + side salad
- Dinner options
  - Salmon + potatoes + asparagus + olive oil
  - Stir-fry: jasmine rice + extra-lean beef/shrimp/tofu + mixed veg + teriyaki
  - Chili bowl: lean beef/turkey + beans + rice + avocado
- Snacks
  - Cottage cheese + pineapple
  - Protein shake + rice cakes with honey
  - Trail mix + fruit
  - Cheese stick + crackers
- Pre-sleep
  - Casein shake or cottage cheese + berries/kiwi
  - Greek yogurt + granola (smaller portion)

7) Weekly check-ins and adjustments (tie to training)
- Track:
  - Average daily bodyweight (morning, after bathroom, before food).
  - Performance markers: top set RPEs, rep PRs, bar speed.
  - Appetite, digestion, sleep quality.
- If lifts are trending up and weight gain is on target: hold macros.
- If performance lags and weight is flat: increase carbs by 25–40 g/day (+100–160 kcal).
- If recovery feels poor or soreness lingers >72 hours: shift more carbs to pre/post-workout windows before raising total calories.

8) Special considerations for combined oral contraceptive (COC)
- No need to phase nutrition across the month; energy needs can be held steady.
- Protein sufficiency and adequate carbs are key for strength/hypertrophy.
- Ensure dietary iron, calcium (1,000 mg/day), and magnesium adequacy; include dairy or fortified alternatives, leafy greens, legumes, and red meat or heme sources if tolerated.

9) Simple 7-day example (for the 65 kg example)
- Daily targets: ~2,450 kcal; P 130 g, F 60 g, C 348 g
- Training days (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri): Keep carbs toward higher end; place ~30–40% of daily carbs across pre/intra/post windows.
- Rest/conditioning days: Same calories (for consistent gain) or −100 kcal if appetite is low; keep protein constant, slightly reduce carbs.

10) Compliance tips
- Build each plate: 1–2 palm portions protein + 1–2 cupped handfuls carbs + 1–2 fists veg + 1–2 thumbs fats.
- Batch-cook carbs and proteins; carry a shaker and fruit for insurance.
- Use a food scale for 1–2 weeks to calibrate portions, then shift to hand-portion estimates if preferred.

With this structure, you can individualize calories and macros to the client’s current bodyweight and update weekly based on bodyweight trend and performance in the program.

Here’s a simple, scalable cardio plan to layer onto the 12-week strength + hypertrophy program for general health without compromising gains. It targets aerobic capacity, cardiac health, and recovery.

Structure
- Frequency: 2–3 cardio sessions/week
- Duration: 20–35 minutes/session (start lower; build gradually)
- Intensity mix:
  - Zone 2 (easy-moderate, conversational pace, RPE 4–5) = foundation
  - Tempo intervals (moderate-hard, RPE 7) = time-efficient stimulus
  - Optional easy recovery work (RPE 3–4) = circulation/mobility

Weekly placement
- Mon: Lower A (no cardio)
- Tue: Upper A (+ optional recovery walk 20–30 min, RPE 3–4)
- Wed: Primary cardio day (Zone 2 or intervals)
- Thu: Lower B (no cardio)
- Fri: Upper B (Optional: short Zone 2)
- Sat: Secondary cardio day (Zone 2)
- Sun: Rest

Modalities (choose 1–2 you enjoy; rotate to spare joints)
- Cycling, incline treadmill walk, easy jog, rowing, elliptical, swimming, rucking (light), jump rope (short bouts), outdoor brisk walks.

12-week progression
- Weeks 1–2:
  - 2 sessions/week.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 25–30 min continuous.
  - Session B: Tempo intervals 6×1 min @ RPE 7 with 2 min easy between; 5–10 min easy warm-up/cooldown.
- Weeks 3–4:
  - 2–3 sessions/week.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 30 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 7–8×1 min @ RPE 7 with 90 s easy.
  - Optional Session C (Fri or Tue): Easy recovery walk 25–30 min, RPE 3–4.
- Weeks 5–6:
  - 2 sessions/week to prioritize strength phase.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 30–35 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 6×90 s @ RPE 7 with 90 s easy (progress from 1-min reps).
- Week 7:
  - 2 sessions.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 30–35 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 5×2 min @ RPE 7 with 2 min easy.
- Week 8:
  - 2 sessions, keep total stress in check pre-deload.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 25–30 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 6×1 min @ RPE 7 with 2 min easy (slight step back).
- Week 9 (Deload):
  - 2 easy sessions only.
  - Both sessions: Zone 2, 20–25 min, RPE 4–5. Skip intervals.
- Week 10:
  - 2–3 sessions.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 30–35 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 6×90 s @ RPE 7 with 90 s easy.
  - Optional Session C: 20–25 min easy walk (RPE 3–4).
- Week 11:
  - 2 sessions.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 30–35 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 5×2 min @ RPE 7 with 2–3 min easy.
- Week 12:
  - 2 sessions, keep fresh for AMRAPs.
  - Session A: Zone 2, 25–30 min.
  - Session B: Intervals 6×1 min @ RPE 7 with 2 min easy.

Warm-up and cooldown (each cardio session)
- Warm-up: 5 min easy ramp + 2–3 short pick-ups (20–30 s at RPE 6) if doing intervals.
- Cooldown: 5 min easy + light mobility (hips, calves, T-spine).

Heart rate anchors (optional, if using a monitor)
- Estimate HRmax = 220 − age ≈ 194 bpm (for a 26-year-old).
- Zone 2 ≈ 60–70% HRmax → ~116–136 bpm.
- Tempo intervals ≈ 80–87% HRmax → ~155–169 bpm.
- Use RPE first; HR is a secondary check.

Progression rules
- If legs feel heavy on lower-body days or strength performance dips: reduce interval volume by 1–2 reps or substitute with Zone 2 that week.
- Prefer low-impact modes (bike/row/elliptical) during heavy squat/deadlift weeks (Weeks 7–8, 10–12).
- Keep at least 24 hours between hard intervals and Lower A/B when possible.

VO2max “top-up” option (swap in once weekly if desired)
- 4×3 min @ RPE 8 (hard but sustainable) with 3 min easy between, total time ≤30–35 min. Use only in Weeks 3–7 if recovery is good.

General health add-ons
- Daily steps: 7,000–10,000.
- Post-lift cooldown walk: 10 minutes easy to aid recovery.
- Outdoor session preference when possible for sunlight exposure and mood.

This cardio plan maintains cardiovascular health and supports recovery while preserving the priority on strength and hypertrophy. Adjust frequency and interval count week-to-week based on lifting performance and perceived fatigue.

Great — here’s an upgraded Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) that pushes intensity and makes use of her good responsiveness while still managing fatigue so Phase 3 can peak well. I’ve added heavier top sets, slight volume trims where appropriate, strategic overload exposures, and tighter progression rules. Everything else in the original plan stays the same unless noted.

Guiding changes for Phase 2
- Compounds: Heavier top sets (1–2 at RPE 8.5–9) followed by strong back-off work. Average intensity ↑, total volume similar or slightly ↓.
- Accessories: Keep quality hypertrophy volume (8–12 reps) but bias slightly heavier loading (RPE 8–9) and reduce to 2 sets on smaller isolation lifts in Week 8 to protect fatigue.
- Recovery: Prefer low-impact cardio in Weeks 7–8; hold intervals if lower-body performance softens.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Intensified Version

Week 5
- Lower A (Squat priority)
  - Back Squat: Top 2×3 @ ~85% (RPE 8.5), then 3×4 @ 80–82%
  - 2-Count Pause Squat: 3×3 @ 72–75%
  - RDL: 3×8 @ RPE 8–9
  - Walking Lunge (DB): 3×10/leg @ RPE 8
  - Leg Curl: 3×10–12 @ RPE 8–9
  - Ab Wheel: 3×8–10
- Upper A (Bench priority)
  - Bench Press: Top 2×3 @ ~85% (RPE 8.5), then 3×4 @ 80–82%
  - 2-Count Paused Bench: 3×3 @ 75%
  - Chest-Supported Row: 4×8 @ RPE 8–9
  - Incline DB Bench: 3×8–10 @ RPE 8
  - Lateral Raise: 3×12–15 @ RPE 8
  - Triceps Pressdown: 3×10–12 @ RPE 8
- Lower B (Deadlift priority)
  - Deadlift: Top 1×3 @ 87–88% (RPE ~9 but clean), then 3×3 @ 82–84%
  - Deficit Deadlift (1–2"): 3×2–3 @ 72–75%
  - Front Squat: 3×4–5 @ RPE 8
  - Hip Thrust: 3×8–10 @ RPE 8–9
  - Back Extension: 3×10–12 @ RPE 8
  - Side Plank: 3×30–45s/side
- Upper B (Overhead/Back priority)
  - Overhead Press: Top 2×2–3 @ 85% (RPE 8.5), then 3×3 @ 80%
  - Push Press: 3×2–3 @ ~80–85% of OHP 1RM-equivalent
  - Pull-Up: 4×6–8 (add load; 1–2 RIR)
  - Single-Arm Cable Row: 3×10/side @ RPE 8–9
  - Face Pull: 3×12–15
  - DB Curl: 3×10–12

Week 6
- Progression targets (if Week 5 top sets ≤RPE 9 and bar speed good):
  - Squat/Bench: +2.5–5 lb (1–2.5 kg) on top sets; match back-off intensity.
  - Deadlift: +5–10 lb (2.5–5 kg) on top set; match back-offs.
  - OHP: +2.5 lb (1 kg) on top sets.
- Session details:
  - Squat: Top 2×3 @ 86–87% (RPE 8.5–9), back-off 3×3–4 @ 82%
  - Bench: Top 2×3 @ 86–87%, back-off 3×3–4 @ 82%
  - Deadlift: Top 1×3 @ 88–89%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 83–85%
  - OHP: Top 2×2–3 @ 86–87%, back-off 3×3 @ 81–82%
- Accessories: Keep RPE 8–9 on compounds’ first accessory (RDL/rows/incline DB), others at RPE 8. If systemic fatigue creeps in, drop last isolation set.

Week 7
- Overreach tilt with guardrails; reduce some accessory sets.
  - Squat: Top 1×2 @ 88–90% (RPE ~9), back-off 3×3 @ 83–85%
  - Bench: Top 1×2 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3 @ 83–85%
  - Deadlift: Top 1×2 @ 90–91% (crisp), back-off 3×2 @ 85%
  - OHP: Top 1×2 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 83–85%
- Secondary variations: Keep but trim volume
  - Pause Squat/Paused Bench: 2×2–3 @ ~75%
  - Deficit Deadlift: 2×2 @ 72–75%
  - Push Press: 2×2 @ ~82–85% of OHP
- Accessories: Big rock accessories 2–3 sets each @ RPE 8–9 (RDL, hip thrust, chest-supported row, incline DB). Isolation (laterals, curls, pressdowns) 2×10–15 @ RPE 8.
- Note: If any top set feels like RPE 9.5 or technique degrades, cut one back-off set that day.

Week 8 (Overload and taper into deload)
- Heaviest exposures of the phase, slight reduction in total sets to control fatigue.
  - Squat: Top 1×2 @ 90–92% (no grinders), back-off 2–3×2–3 @ 85%
  - Bench: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 2–3×2–3 @ 85%
  - Deadlift: Top 1×1–2 @ 92–93% (smooth single or strong double), back-off 2–3×2 @ 85–87%
  - OHP: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 2–3×2 @ 85%
- Variations: Keep to 1–2 light sets (technique primers only) at ~70–72%.
- Accessories: Limit to 1–2 key movements per session, 2×8–12 @ RPE 7–8 to keep fitness without adding fatigue.
- Recovery emphasis: Extra sleep, low-impact cardio only (Zone 2 20–25 min), mobility.

Load and autoregulation rules for the intensified phase
- If top set RPE <8.5 with clean form, add load the next week within the suggested jumps.
- If top set hits RPE 9.5 or bar speed notably slows, hold the load and reduce one back-off set, or drop 2.5% on back-offs.
- Back-off intensity should feel like strong work but not grindy; keep 1–2 reps in reserve.
- Technique trumps load. No failed reps.

Cardio adjustments for Weeks 5–8
- Keep 2 sessions/week.
- Prefer bike/row/elliptical.
- During Weeks 7–8, skip intervals if legs feel heavy; do 25–30 min Zone 2 instead.

Nutrition nudge for the push phase
- On squat/deadlift days in Weeks 6–8, bias carbs upward by +25–50 g on those days (from the base plan) to support performance and recovery.
- Keep creatine daily; consider caffeine at 1.5–3 mg/kg pre-lift if tolerated.

Here’s how to add one dedicated HIIT day without derailing strength/hypertrophy. We’ll place it midweek, dose it conservatively at first, and periodize it across the 12 weeks. Use low-impact modes (bike/row/ski erg) to spare knees/hips during heavy lower-body phases.

Placement
- Primary HIIT day: Wednesday
- Keep ≥24 hours away from Lower A (Mon) and Lower B (Thu)
- Replace the prior “tempo intervals” day with this HIIT session. Keep one additional Zone 2 session on Saturday (or Friday after Upper B).

General rules
- Modality: Air bike, spin bike, rower, or ski erg preferred. If running, use hills or soft surfaces.
- Warm-up: 8–10 min easy + 3 strides/accelerations (20–30 s at RPE 6) + 3–5 mobility drills.
- Effort caps: Hard intervals at RPE 8–9 (breathing heavy, still in control). No all-out sprints.
- Volume caps: Total hard work time 8–16 minutes depending on week/phase.
- Cooldown: 5–8 min easy + light mobility.
- If lower-body fatigue lingers into Thu squats/deads, cut the next HIIT week’s reps by 20–30% or switch to Zone 2.

12-week HIIT progression
- Weeks 1–2 (on-ramp)
  - Option A (bike/row): 10×30 s hard (RPE 8–9) / 60 s easy
  - Option B (if you prefer longer reps): 6×45 s hard / 75 s easy
  - Total hard time: 5–7.5 min
- Weeks 3–4 (build)
  - 12×30 s hard / 60 s easy, or 8×45 s hard / 75 s easy
  - Total hard time: 6–9 min
- Weeks 5–6 (intensify; strength phase ramps)
  - 8×60 s hard (RPE 8.5–9) / 90 s easy
  - Total hard time: 8 min
  - Note: Prefer bike/row to spare joints
- Week 7 (overreach tilt; keep quality)
  - 6×75 s hard / 2 min easy
  - Total hard time: 7.5 min
- Week 8 (hold intensity, trim volume pre-deload)
  - 8×45 s hard / 90 s easy
  - Total hard time: 6 min
- Week 9 (deload)
  - Swap HIIT for steady Zone 2: 20–25 min at RPE 4–5
- Week 10 (rebuild)
  - 10×45 s hard / 75 s easy
  - Total hard time: 7.5 min
- Week 11 (peak quality)
  - 6×60 s hard / 2 min easy
  - Total hard time: 6 min
- Week 12 (taper for AMRAPs)
  - 6×30 s hard / 90 s easy, keep it snappy, not maximal
  - Total hard time: 3 min

Optional alternative (VO2 “3-minute” set, swap in 1 of every 3 weeks if recovery is great)
- 4×3 min @ RPE 8 (hard but even pace) / 3 min easy, total work 12 min. Use bike/row. Do not use in Weeks 7–8 or Week 12.

Technique and safety cues
- Aim for consistent power across reps (track watts/pace); avoid a massive drop-off after the first intervals.
- Stay seated on bike sprints to protect low back/hips.
- Maintain tall posture on rower; drive with legs first, then hinge and pull.
- Stop a rep early if form degrades; quality beats quantity.

Fueling and recovery
- Pre-HIIT: 20–40 g carbs + 15–25 g protein 60–120 min before.
- Post-HIIT: 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 1–2 hours.
- Hydration: 300–500 ml with electrolytes if sweating heavily.
- If HIIT performance tanks or legs feel heavy for Thu Lower B, cut next week’s HIIT work by 25–50% or do Zone 2 instead.

Weekly layout with HIIT integrated
- Mon: Lower A (no cardio)
- Tue: Upper A (optional 20–30 min easy walk)
- Wed: HIIT (as above)
- Thu: Lower B
- Fri: Upper B (optional 20–25 min Zone 2)
- Sat: Zone 2, 25–35 min
- Sun: Rest

This gives you a clear, progressive HIIT day that boosts fitness and health with minimal interference to strength and hypertrophy progress. Adjust interval count week-to-week based on barbell performance and perceived fatigue.

2) Plyo + power block (20–25 min)
- Sequencing: low-amplitude elastic → extensive jumps → intensive jumps → med-ball throws. Rest 60–120 s between sets.

- Overhead backward throw 3×3–4 (if space allows)

4) Cooldown (5 min)
- Easy bike/walk + calf/hip flexor/hamstring mobility.

Weekly progression across 12 weeks
- Weeks 1–2 (on-ramp; 40–50 contacts, 12–16 throws)
  - A: Pogo jumps 2×25
  - B: Squat jumps 3×6
  - C: Box jumps 3×4 + Skater bounds 3×4/side

Here’s a safe, structured 1RM test plan at the end of Phase 3 to gauge progress without derailing recovery. We’ll use a short taper in Week 12 and test across two days in Week 13. If you prefer to keep everything inside 12 weeks, see the “Same-week option” at the end.

Goal lifts
- Back squat, bench press, conventional deadlift, overhead press (barbell)

Scheduling
- Week 12 (taper): Keep the programmed AMRAPs but reduce accessory volume to minimal pump work and keep HIIT/plyos light as previously outlined.
- Week 13 (test week):
  - Day 1 (Mon): Squat + Bench 1RM tests
  - Day 2 (Tue): Rest or light mobility walk 20–30 min
  - Day 3 (Wed): Deadlift + Overhead Press 1RM tests
  - The rest of the week: Easy recovery, then resume normal training the following Monday with new training maxes (85–90% of tested 1RMs) for the next cycle.

General rules for test days
- Sleep 7–9 h; normal caffeine. Eat your usual surplus with extra carbs the night before and 60–120 min pre-lift.
- Warm-up thoroughly; no static stretching that reduces stiffness pre-lift.
- Use consistent equipment, footwear, rack heights, and judging standards (hip crease below knee for squat, pause at chest for bench if that’s how you train, deadlift lockout with control, OHP without leg drive).
- Stop testing a lift if bar speed falls dramatically or technique breaks down. No grinders beyond RPE 9.5.
- Have safety pins or spotters for squat/bench.

Standardized warm-up for each 1RM attempt
- General: 5–8 min light cardio, dynamic hips/shoulders/ankles/T-spine
- Specific ramp (example percentages of an estimated 1RM; adjust by RPE/bar speed)
  - 5 reps @ 30–40%
  - 3 reps @ 50%
  - 2 reps @ 60%
  - 1 rep @ 70%
  - 1 rep @ 77–80%
  - 1 rep @ 85%
  - 1 rep @ 90% (first “real” gauge rep)
  - Then 1–3 single attempts as needed

Attempt selection and jumps
- Use Week 12 AMRAPs to estimate updated 1RMs (Epley or RIR-based) and set your openers accordingly.
- Squat and deadlift
  - Opener: ~90–92% of estimated 1RM (should feel like a fast single; confidence builder)
  - Second: 96–99% based on opener speed
  - Third: 100–103% if second was clean; otherwise repeat or take a small PR (0.5–1.0%).
  - Typical jumps: 10–20 lb (5–10 kg) depending on lifter strength level and bar speed.
- Bench press and overhead press
  - Opener: 90–92%
  - Second: 96–99%
  - Third: 100–102% (upper body lifts often like smaller jumps)
  - Typical jumps: 2.5–10 lb (1–5 kg), smaller for OHP.

Bar-speed guidance (if using a velocity tracker; optional)
- Opener: ≥0.35–0.45 m/s for squat/dead; ≥0.20–0.25 m/s for bench/OHP
- If second attempt speed drops below ~0.20 m/s (squat/dead) or ~0.12 m/s (bench/OHP), cap the day or repeat a weight for a clean make rather than forcing a grinder.

Test day structure (Day 1: Squat + Bench)
- Warm-up to squat opener using the ramp above; take attempts 1–3 with 3–5 min rest between.
- After final squat, rest 10–15 min, light shoulder/band work, then ramp bench using similar steps (you can skip the earliest warm-up sets if already warm).
- Accessories: None, or 1–2 light pump sets (e.g., leg curls, face pulls) only if desired.

Test day structure (Day 3: Deadlift + OHP)
- Warm-up to deadlift opener; take attempts with 4–6 min rest.
- Rest 10–15 min before OHP; keep warm-up volumes minimal.

Safety and standards
- Squat: Depth below parallel; controlled descent; no heaving/sliding on the rack; stance and bar placement consistent with training.
- Bench: Feet set, butt/shoulders on bench, brief pause on chest, no heave or downward movement after press command (if self-judging, count “one-Mississippi”).
- Deadlift: Controlled start, no hitching, full lockout, controlled return.
- OHP: Strict—no leg drive; lockout with elbows/shoulders stacked.

Taper and readiness checklist (Week 12 into Week 13)
- Keep Week 12 AMRAPs submaximal caps as written; skip any extra isolation work the rest of that week.
- HIIT: Perform the short taper session (6×30 s) early in Week 12 or skip if legs are heavy.
- Plyometrics: Use the Week 12 low-contact template; skip the optional power primer.
- Steps: Normal. Sleep: Aim top end (8–9 h).
- Carb-up: Add 50–100 g extra carbs the evening before each test day; normal sodium hydration.

Data capture and next-cycle targets
- Record: Each attempt load, RPE, bar speed (if available), and any form notes.
- Derive new training maxes at 85–90% of true 1RM for the next cycle to keep submax strength work crisp.
- Accessory loads can be nudged up 2–5% next cycle if hypertrophy is still a goal and recovery is solid.

Same-week option (if you must finish within 12 weeks)
- Replace Week 12 AMRAPs with test singles:
  - Day 1 (Mon): Squat + Bench tests
  - Day 3 (Thu): Deadlift + OHP tests
- In Week 11, keep the top singles at ~90% instead of pushing; reduce accessory volume by 30–40% to be fresher.
- Keep HIIT very light in Week 12 or skip it.

This plan gives you clean, repeatable testing conditions with minimal risk and high signal-to-noise so you can confidently gauge progress and set loads for the next block.

Here’s the complete 12-week strength + hypertrophy program starting 2026-06-01, with all adjustments integrated: intensified Phase 2, added cardio (including a dedicated HIIT day), a weekly plyometric/power session, a hypertrophy-supportive nutrition plan, and a post-cycle 1RM test week. Layout uses a 6-day structure (4 lifts + HIIT + Plyo/Power) with one full rest day.

Global structure
- Training days: Mon Lower A, Tue Upper A, Wed HIIT, Thu Lower B, Fri Upper B, Sat Plyo/Power, Sun Rest
- Conditioning: HIIT on Wed; Zone 2 on Sat optional after plyos or on Fri post-Upper B (light)
- Deload: Week 9
- Phases: P1 Weeks 1–4 Hypertrophy base; P2 Weeks 5–8 Strength Intensified; P3 Weeks 9–12 Intensification/Taper with AMRAP caps
- 1RM testing: Week 13 (Days 1 and 3)

General session standards
- Warm-up: 5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility + specific ramp-up sets for compounds
- Rest: Compounds 2–4 min; accessories 60–90 s
- Tempo: Controlled 2–3 s eccentrics on accessories; crisp but controlled on compounds
- RPE/RIR: Compounds as prescribed; accessories RPE 7–9 with 1–2 RIR
- Progression rules:
  - Main lifts: If all prescribed reps done ≤RPE 8.5, add 1–2.5 kg (upper body) or 2.5–5 kg (lower body) next exposure. If RPE ≥9.5 or form degrades, hold or reduce 2.5–5% and trim one back-off set.
  - Accessories: Double progression—add 1–2 reps within range before adding the smallest load the following week.

WEEK-BY-WEEK PLAN

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07) — Phase 1
- Mon Lower A (Squat focus)
  - Back Squat 4×6 @ ~70% (RPE 7–8)
  - Romanian Deadlift 3×8 @ RPE 7–8
  - DB Split Squat 3×10/side @ RPE 8
  - Seated/Leg Curl 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Standing Calf Raise 3×12–15 @ RPE 8
  - Core: Hanging Knee Raise 3×10–12
- Tue Upper A (Bench focus)
  - Barbell Bench Press 4×6 @ ~70% (RPE 7–8)
  - One-Arm DB Row 3×10/side @ RPE 8
  - Incline DB Bench 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown 3×10–12 @ RPE 8
  - Cable Lateral Raise 3×12–15 @ RPE 8
  - Triceps Rope Pressdown 2–3×12
- Wed HIIT
  - 10×30 s hard (RPE 8–9) / 60 s easy on bike/row (8–10 min warm-up, 5–8 min cooldown)
- Thu Lower B (Hinge focus)
  - Conventional Deadlift 4×4 @ 72–75% (RPE 7–8)
  - Front Squat 3×6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Barbell Hip Thrust 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - 45° Back Extension 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Seated Calf Raise 3×12–15
  - Core: Pallof Press 3×10–12/side
- Fri Upper B (OHP/Row focus)
  - Overhead Press 4×5 @ ~70% (RPE 7–8)
  - Pull-Up or Assisted 4×6–8 (2 RIR)
  - Chest-Supported Row 3×10 @ RPE 8
  - DB Incline Fly or Cable Fly 3×12 @ RPE 8
  - Face Pull 3×12–15
  - EZ-Bar Curl 2–3×10–12
- Sat Plyometric/Power Day
  - Warm-up: 5–10 min + pogo hops 2×20, A-skips 2×20 m
  - Pogo 2×25; Squat Jumps 3×6; Box Jumps 3×4 (step down) + Skater Bounds 3×4/side
  - Med-ball: Chest Pass 3×5 + Scoop Toss 3×4/side
  - Optional: KB Swing 3×8 @ RPE 7
  - Optional Zone 2: 15–20 min easy
- Sun Rest

Week 2 — Phase 1
- Lifts: Nudge loads 2.5% on compounds if Week 1 ≤RPE 8 or add 1 rep to first set; accessories add 1–2 reps or small load.
- HIIT: 10×30 s hard/60 s easy (or 6×45 s/75 s easy)
- Plyo/Power: Same template; maintain quality
- Keep Zone 2 optional (15–25 min) on Sat post-plyo or Fri after Upper B

Week 3 — Phase 1 Build
- Mon Squat 4×7 @ 72–73% (RPE 8); RDL 3×8; keep accessories progressing
- Tue Bench 4×6–7 @ 72–73%; rows/pulldowns 3–4×10–12
- Wed HIIT: 12×30 s/60 s easy OR 8×45 s/75 s easy
- Thu Deadlift 4×5 @ 75–77%; Front Squat 3×6; Hip Thrust 3×10
- Fri OHP 4×6 @ 72–73%; Pull-Ups 4×6–8; Rows/face pulls/laterals/curls
- Sat Plyo/Power (build)
  - Line Hops 2×30; Broad Jumps 3×4–5; Hurdle Hops (low) 3×3–4 + Split Squat Jumps 3×3/side
  - Med-ball Rotational Scoop 4×4/side
  - Optional Trap Bar Jump Shrug 3×3 @ 20–25%
- Sun Rest

Week 4 — Phase 1 Overreach-lite
- Mon Squat 5×6 @ 72–75% (top set ≤RPE 8.5)
- Tue Bench 5×6 @ 72–75%
- Wed HIIT: 12×30 s/60 s easy (or 8×45 s/75 s)
- Thu Deadlift 5×4 @ 77–78%
- Fri OHP 5×5 @ 73–75%; accessories steady (don’t chase failure)
- Sat Plyo/Power hold: Pogo 2×20; Seated Box Jump 3×4; Box Jump 3×3 + Skater Bounds 2–3×4/side; Med-ball Chest Pass 3×5
- Sun Rest

Week 5 — Phase 2 Intensified (good responder)
- Mon Lower A (Squat priority)
  - Back Squat: Top 2×3 @ ~85% (RPE 8.5), then 3×4 @ 80–82%
  - 2-Count Pause Squat 3×3 @ 72–75%
  - RDL 3×8 @ RPE 8–9
  - DB Walking Lunge 3×10/leg
  - Leg Curl 3×10–12
  - Ab Wheel 3×8–10
- Tue Upper A (Bench priority)
  - Bench: Top 2×3 @ ~85%, then 3×4 @ 80–82%
  - 2-Count Paused Bench 3×3 @ ~75%
  - Chest-Supported Row 4×8 @ RPE 8–9
  - Incline DB Bench 3×8–10
  - Lateral Raise 3×12–15
  - Triceps Pressdown 3×10–12
- Wed HIIT
  - 8×60 s hard (RPE 8.5–9) / 90 s easy (bike/row preferred)
- Thu Lower B (Deadlift priority)
  - Deadlift: Top 1×3 @ 87–88% (clean), then 3×3 @ 82–84%
  - Deficit Deadlift 3×2–3 @ 72–75%
  - Front Squat 3×4–5 @ RPE 8
  - Hip Thrust 3×8–10 @ RPE 8–9
  - Back Extension 3×10–12
  - Side Plank 3×30–45 s/side
- Fri Upper B (OHP/Back)
  - OHP: Top 2×2–3 @ 85%, then 3×3 @ 80%
  - Push Press 3×2–3 @ ~80–85% OHP equiv
  - Pull-Up 4×6–8 (add load; 1–2 RIR)
  - Single-Arm Cable Row 3×10/side @ RPE 8–9
  - Face Pull 3×12–15
  - DB Curl 3×10–12
- Sat Plyo/Power (intensify)
  - Pogo 3×20; Seated Box Jump 3×4
  - Box Jump (20–24") 4×3 + Skater Bounds 3×5/side
  - OH Backward Throw 4×3 + Chest Pass 2×5
  - Optional: Speed Squat 5×2 @ 55–60% (only if fresh)
- Sun Rest

Week 6 — Phase 2 Progress
- Progress loads per rules (+1–5 kg if Week 5 top sets ≤RPE 9, bar speed good)
- Mon Squat: Top 2×3 @ 86–87%, back-off 3×3–4 @ ~82%
- Tue Bench: Top 2×3 @ 86–87%, back-off 3×3–4 @ ~82%
- Wed HIIT: 8×60 s hard / 90 s easy
- Thu Deadlift: Top 1×3 @ 88–89%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 83–85%
- Fri OHP: Top 2×2–3 @ 86–87%, back-off 3×3 @ 81–82%
- Accessories: Keep big rocks RPE 8–9; trim an isolation set if fatigue rises
- Sat Plyo/Power: Same as Week 5 or swap med-ball emphasis to Rotational Scoop 4×4/side
- Nutrition note: Add +25–50 g carbs on Mon/Thu training days

Week 7 — Phase 2 Overreach Tilt (quality first)
- Mon Squat: Top 1×2 @ 88–90% (RPE ~9), back-off 3×3 @ 83–85%; Pause Squat 2×2–3 @ ~75%
- Tue Bench: Top 1×2 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3 @ 83–85%; Paused Bench 2×2–3 @ ~75%
- Wed HIIT: 6×75 s hard / 2 min easy (or reduce to Zone 2 25–30 min if legs heavy)
- Thu Deadlift: Top 1×2 @ 90–91%, back-off 3×2 @ 85%; Deficit DL 2×2 @ 72–75%
- Fri OHP: Top 1×2 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 83–85%; Push Press 2×2 @ 82–85%
- Accessories: Keep only key accessories 2–3 sets @ RPE 8–9; isolation 2×10–15
- Sat Plyo/Power (overreach quality)
  - Ankle Dribbles 3×12 m; Broad Jumps 3×4–5
  - Depth Drops to Stick 3×3 (12–18") + Split Squat Jumps 3×3/side
  - Rotational Scoop Toss 4×4/side
  - Optional: KB Swing 4×8 @ RPE 7
- Sun Rest

Week 8 — Phase 2 Heaviest Exposures, Volume Trim
- Mon Squat: Top 1×2 @ 90–92% (no grinders), back-off 2–3×2–3 @ ~85%
- Tue Bench: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 2–3×2–3 @ ~85%
- Wed HIIT: 8×45 s hard / 90 s easy (keep fresh)
- Thu Deadlift: Top 1×1–2 @ 92–93%, back-off 2–3×2 @ 85–87%
- Fri OHP: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 2–3×2 @ ~85%
- Accessories: Limit to 1–2 key moves/session, 2×8–12 @ RPE 7–8
- Sat Plyo/Power (reduced)
  - Pogo 2×20; Seated Box Jump 3×3–4
  - Box Jump 3×3 + Skater Bounds 2×4/side
  - Chest Pass 3×5; skip optional primer
- Sun Rest

Week 9 — Phase 3 Deload
- Mon Squat 3×3 @ 60–65%
- Tue Bench 3×3 @ 60–65%
- Wed Cardio: Swap HIIT for Zone 2, 20–25 min @ RPE 4–5
- Thu Deadlift 3×2 @ 60–65%
- Fri OHP 3×3 @ 60–65%; accessories 1–2 light sets each @ RPE 6–7
- Sat Plyo/Power (light): Pogo 2×20; Squat Jump 2×5; Box Jump (low) 2×3; Light Chest Pass 2×5
- Sun Rest

Week 10 — Phase 3 Top Set + Back-Off
- Mon Squat: Top 1×3 @ 85–88% (RPE ~8.5), then 3×4 @ ~80%; Quad accessory 2–3×8–10
- Tue Bench: Top 1×3 @ 85–88%, then 3×4 @ ~80%; Row 2–3×8–10; Incline DB 2–3×8–10
- Wed HIIT: 10×45 s hard / 75 s easy (or 6×60 s / 2 min easy if preferred)
- Thu Deadlift: Top 1×2–3 @ 87–90%, then 3×3 @ 80–82%; Hamstring accessory 2–3×10–12
- Fri OHP: Top 1×3 @ 85%, then 3×4 @ 78–80%; Pull-ups 3–4×6–8 (1–2 RIR); Laterals/arms 2×12–15
- Sat Plyo/Power (rebuild): Pogo 2×25; Broad Jumps 3×4; Hurdle Hops (low) 3×3 + Skater Bounds 3×4/side; Rotational Scoop 4×4/side; Optional Trap Bar Jump Shrug 3×3 @ 20–25%
- Sun Rest

Week 11 — Phase 3 Progress
- Mon Squat: Top 1×2–3 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3–4 @ 80–82%
- Tue Bench: Top 1×2–3 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×3–4 @ 80–82%
- Wed HIIT: 6×60 s hard / 2 min easy (cap total stress)
- Thu Deadlift: Top 1×2 @ 90–92%, back-off 3×2–3 @ 82–85%
- Fri OHP: Top 1×2–3 @ 87–88%, back-off 3×3 @ 80–82%
- Accessories: Same light-to-moderate approach, 1–2 RIR
- Sat Plyo/Power (peak quality): Pogo 3×20; Seated Box Jump 3×4; Box Jump 3×3–4 + Split Squat Jumps 3×3/side; OH Throw 3×3 + Chest Pass 2×5; Optional Speed Squat 4×2 @ 50–55% if very fresh
- Sun Rest

Week 12 — Phase 3 Taper + AMRAP Caps
- Mon Squat: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% (cap 5–6 reps, stop at RPE 9), then 2×3 @ ~80%; minimal accessories
- Tue Bench: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% (cap 6–7), then 2×3 @ ~80%
- Wed HIIT (taper): 6×30 s hard / 90 s easy OR skip if legs heavy
- Thu Deadlift: 1×AMRAP @ ~85% (cap 4–5), then 2×2 @ ~80%
- Fri OHP: 1×AMRAP @ 82–85% (cap 5–6), then 2×3 @ 78–80%
- Sat Plyo/Power (taper): Pogo 2×20; Box Jump 2×3 (moderate box); Skater Bounds 2×4/side; Chest Pass 2×5
- Sun Rest

Week 13 — 1RM Test Week (to gauge progress)
- Day 1 Mon: Squat + Bench 1RM tests
  - Standard ramp: 5@40%, 3@50%, 2@60%, 1@70%, 1@80%, 1@85%, 1@90%, then attempts
  - Attempts: Opener 90–92%, Second 96–99% (based on speed), Third 100–103% if clean
- Day 2 Tue: Rest or 20–30 min easy walk/mobility
- Day 3 Wed: Deadlift + OHP 1RM tests (same ramp/attempt logic; smaller jumps for OHP)
- Post: Easy recovery Thu–Sun; set next-cycle training maxes to 85–90% of true 1RMs

Cardio plan (integrated)
- HIIT: As detailed weekly on Wednesdays
- Zone 2: Optional 15–35 min after Sat plyos (keep easy) or Fri post-Upper B. In deload Week 9, do 20–25 min Zone 2 on Wed (no HIIT)
- Daily steps: 7,000–10,000; 10-min easy walk post-lift if time permits

Plyometric/Power plan (integrated)
- Dedicated Saturday session with progressive contact counts and med-ball throws as laid out each week; avoid hard surfaces; land softly; stop sets when quality drops

Nutrition plan for hypertrophy (daily, with training-day tweaks)
- Calories: Maintenance +200–300 kcal/day; target ~0.25–0.5% bodyweight gain/week
- Macros:
  - Protein 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day (range 1.6–2.2)
  - Fat 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day (not below 0.7)
  - Carbs: Fill remainder (typically 3–6 g/kg/day in surplus)
  - Fiber: 25–35 g/day
- Timing:
  - Pre-lift (1–2 h): 30–60 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; low fat/fiber
  - Post-lift (0–2 h): 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein
  - Pre-sleep: 20–40 g casein-rich protein
- Supplements:
  - Creatine 3–5 g/day
  - Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU/day if needed
  - Fish oil 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if intake low
  - Caffeine 1.5–3 mg/kg pre-workout if desired
- Phase 2 carb nudge: On Mon/Thu (heavy lower), add +25–50 g carbs those days
- Weekly adjustments:
  - If weight gain <0.15% BW/week for 2 weeks and performance good: +80–120 kcal/day
  - If >0.6% BW/week for 2 weeks or recovery worsens: −80–120 kcal/day
- Micronutrients: Ensure calcium ~1,000 mg/day, iron, and magnesium adequacy
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day + 500–1,000 ml around training; electrolytes in heat

Recovery and autoregulation
- Sleep: 7–9 h/night; aim 8–9 h in Weeks 7–8 and 12–13
- Mobility: 8–12 min daily (hips, T-spine, ankles, shoulders)
- Readiness checks: If two consecutive sessions feel ≥2 points worse than baseline, cut accessory volume by 20–30% that week
- Stalls: If a lift stalls 2 weeks, drop 5% and rebuild
- Technique: Prioritize full ROM, bracing, and bar path; no grinders outside of Week 12 AMRAP caps and Week 13 testing

This consolidated plan gives you a precise, week-by-week roadmap with heavier Phase 2 exposures, integrated HIIT and plyometrics, nutrition for hypertrophy, and a clear post-cycle 1RM test to quantify progress. Adjust loads each week using RPE and the progression rules to fit day-to-day readiness.
